finalText:
Migration finished. 12 first-party files converted (36 call sites), all syntax-checked clean:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `service/teamService.js`, `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| orders | `service/returnService.js`, `repo/shipment.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| billing | `service/couponService.js`, `repo/refund.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the shape used by the already-migrated files.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — still on `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost. Editing it would be undone by the next upgrade. Since `lib/db.js` notes the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix — upstream patch, or a wrapper that adapts the vendored calls — rather than an in-place edit. Flagging it as the one remaining blocker.
- **`cache.query(...)`** across ~20 repo files — that's `lib/cache.js`, an unrelated API, not part of this migration.

`db.query` is still defined in `lib/db.js`; you can't delete it until the vendor case is resolved.
